about.label: About Me
about.title: Curious about me? Here you have it.
about.description:
I'm a Tech Lead and Mobile Engineer with 4+ years of experience building Android, iOS, desktop, web, SDK, and hardware-connected clinical systems across healthcare, government, industrial, education, retail, and enterprise domains. My recent work focuses on Kotlin Multiplatform, Jetpack Compose, Clean Architecture, USB/BLE medical device integrations, offline-first workflows, and production systems used in hospital environments across Southeast Asia.

I have led 5+ engineers, shipped 5+ medical applications, supported 10+ USB/BLE medical devices, and partnered closely with product, design, firmware, backend, and client teams to turn complex clinical requirements into reliable release-ready software. I also hold a Bachelor's degree in Informatics Engineering from Universitas Dian Nuswantoro with a 3.83 / 4.00 GPA, and I keep a strong engineering bias toward maintainable architecture, testing, CI/CD, mentoring, and practical product delivery.

experience.label: Experience
experience.title: Here is a quick summary of my most recent experiences:

items.title: Tech Lead, Software Team
responsibilities: Led 5+ engineers across mobile, desktop, and web platforms, delivering 5+ hardware-connected medical applications used across hospitals in Southeast Asia.
Coordinated 10+ USB/BLE medical device integrations with firmware, product, design, backend, and client teams, translating clinical requirements into production-ready workflows.
Researched and proposed offline-first architecture for clinical device applications, improving workflow continuity, sync recovery, and device reliability during unstable hospital network conditions.

items.title: Mobile Engineer
responsibilities: Delivered production mobile apps connected to 5+ USB/BLE medical devices, enabling live streaming, calibration, and remote control for clinical workflows.
Built reusable modules for BLE GATT, real-time video, offline handling, retry flows, and on-device ML, accelerating hardware integration and rollout across medical device products.
Partnered with firmware and backend teams to define protocols, harden failure states, and ship resilient clinic-ready applications.

items.title: iOS Developer, Contract
responsibilities: Shipped end-to-end iOS features using Clean Architecture and MVVM in Swift, supported by unit and UI test suites to improve release confidence and reduce production regressions.
Implemented Superwall Paywall end-to-end on iOS, including a 5-second delayed trial prompt that improved purchase intent and increased conversion by ~70%.

items.title: Android Engineer Intern
responsibilities: Refactored legacy modules and resolved production bugs in the Traveloka Android app with 50M+ downloads, improving responsiveness across device tiers and strengthening release stability.
Delivered Android features using Clean MVVM and MVP in Kotlin and Java, increased unit/UI test coverage to 70%+, and reduced release regressions.
Researched Jetpack Compose adoption and modern Android library integration to improve UI performance and developer efficiency.

items.title: Mobile Developer
responsibilities: Designed, built, and shipped 20+ mobile apps across education and retail using Kotlin/Java (Android) and Flutter (cross-platform).
Led a 4-person team, ran Agile sprints, coordinated cross-functionally, and standardized CI/CD across GitHub, GitLab, and CircleCI.
Built RESTful API backends using Node.js and Laravel to support authentication, real-time updates, and secure data storage for mobile products.

items.title: Mobile Developer Intern
responsibilities: Delivered Android features in Kotlin with Firebase Realtime Database (live updates) and Crashlytics (instrumentation, alerting), reducing repeat crash types during the program.
Practiced version control (Git) and participated in collaborative code reviews as part of a remote internship program simulating real-world development environments.

projects.label: Projects
projects.title: Some of the projects I’ve worked on:

items.stethoscope_project: The Stethoscope app is a Kotlin Multiplatform application built with Jetpack Compose, running natively on Android and iOS from a single shared codebase. It pairs with BLE-enabled stethoscopes to stream high-fidelity heart and lung sounds and visualize them in real time. Devices that support a USB connection can also be wired in directly for more stable, latency-free audio streaming. Recordings are attached to patient encounters for longitudinal tracking, and the offline-first data layer keeps sessions intact even without a network connection.
items.xray_project: The 8xray app is a Kotlin Multiplatform application built with Jetpack Compose, running natively on Android, iOS, and Desktop from a single shared codebase. It communicates with X-ray hardware through native DLL and SO libraries, giving direct access to device controls, real-time image acquisition, and calibration routines at the hardware level. The app pulls DICOM studies, lets doctors label findings, draw regions of interest, measure angles and distances, and fine-tune contrast and window or level using an OpenCV-powered toolkit. Everything follows an offline-first model: studies, edits, and notes are stored locally and synced back to the backend when a connection is available, so rounds and consultations are never interrupted by network conditions.
items.digihealth_kiosk_project: The Health Kiosk is a Kotlin Multiplatform application built with Jetpack Compose, running natively on Android, iOS, and Desktop from a single shared codebase. Deployed inside Digihealth ATM units in clinics and hospitals, it provides a self-service healthcare experience where patients can log in, join queues, schedule appointments, and review medical records. The kiosk connects to 10+ medical devices over BLE and USB, including weight scales, height sensors, oximeters, blood pressure monitors, and thermometers, collecting real-time vitals in a single session. AI modules handle health risk prediction, symptom triage, and intelligent recommendations based on the collected data. Shared domain logic covers device protocols, data synchronization, and offline queuing, while Compose Multiplatform renders a consistent, clinic-ready UI across all platforms.
items.patient_health_companion_project: The Patient Health Companion is a Flutter mobile app that brings the Digihealth kiosk experience to phones. It runs on Android and iOS with the same look and feel. The interface is clean and easy to tap. Patients can update their profile and health data. They can view or book appointments without calling the clinic. Video and chat visits work inside the app using Agora, with simple layouts that keep notes and messages visible. Daily tracking covers vitals, nutrition, sleep, and fitness goals. The app turns these inputs into clear trends and practical tips, with AI insights shown only when they help. The Companion connects to the Digihealth backend through secure REST APIs and WebSockets for live updates. Appointments, messages, and measurements stay in sync across kiosk and mobile. It feels like one continuous place for care at home, on the move, and in the clinic.
items.teddy_project: Released in Traveloka 1.1.1. I reworked ticket details to surface what travelers actually compare: baggage and change/refund rules, fare differences, seating and timing notes, and clear vendor terms in plain language. The layout prioritizes must-know info above the fold and reduces jargon, so users feel confident and move forward without bouncing between tabs.
items.tweety_project: Released in Traveloka 4.0.0. I updated a lot of pieces, from the carousel to ticket descriptions. I added a “Browse other tickets” section inside the ticket detail so users can check better times or prices without losing their place. Each alternative shows time differences, fare rules, seats left, baggage, and change or refund info, with quick sort and filter controls and clear comparison chips. I also tightened the booking flow from listing to attendee selection with smarter defaults and prefills, clearer step progress, and stronger error handling. The result is fewer interruptions and a smoother path to payment.
items.lp_sr_cruise_project: Released in Traveloka 4.0.0. I introduced multi-select filters with dependency logic. When a user chooses a filter, the remaining options update to show only valid combinations, with removable chips, preserved state across pagination, and deep-linkable URLs. This makes exploration faster and avoids dead-end results.
items.spaceAttack_kmp_swiftui: Arcade shooter I wrote once and shipped to iOS and Android. The core loop, scoring rules, and leaderboard logic live in Kotlin Multiplatform so fixes land in both apps. SwiftUI and Compose handle the UI with the same timing constants, so animations feel identical at 60 fps. Saves are local for fast resume and a small sync runs in the background when the network is available. I split the code into MVVM modules so gameplay, storage, and network do not leak into each other. The project is a good template for small cross platform games that want native UI.
items.stasave_compose: Status saver with a clean Compose surface and very few steps. It scans media folders, builds a fast thumbnail grid, and writes files with WorkManager so downloads keep going even if the app is backgrounded. The permission flow is short and direct, and a storage cleaner removes temporary bits after a successful save. I added a share action and a small snackbar system so users get immediate feedback. The codebase follows a simple MVVM pattern and each screen has a preview for quick UI review.
items.beritain_swiftui: SwiftUI news reader that stays responsive on a slow connection. Articles are cached in Core Data and images are loaded with an async pipeline so scrolling stays smooth. I used Swinject for dependency injection to keep view code light. The layout supports multiple languages and I validated a few tricky truncation cases. CI runs SwiftLint and unit tests on each push, and a background refresh updates headlines while the app is idle.
items.leech_android_lib: Small Android download library that focuses on reliability. It wraps OkHttp, supports pause and resume, and handles flaky networks with simple retry rules. A foreground service shows progress and survives configuration changes. The API has clear entry points and the sample app doubles as a test bed with edge cases like server redirects and partial content. I kept the surface small so teams can adopt it without pulling in a lot of extra code.
items.floating_menu_ios: Floating action menu for iOS shipped as a Swift Package. It anchors to a tab bar or a custom container and adjusts to safe areas automatically. Haptics are built in, light and dark mode are supported, and spacing and icons can be tuned with a few parameters. I paid attention to animation timing so the menu feels quick without being jumpy. The demo targets a couple of screen sizes to make sure the layout stays tidy.
items.highlightor_android_lib: Compose utility for guided walkthroughs and onboarding. It measures target bounds at runtime, dims the rest of the screen, and steps through a sequence with a builder style API. Touch is blocked outside the focus area, and the arrow and label can be themed. I tested a few gesture heavy screens to confirm it does not break scroll or fling. The code is small enough that teams can read it in one sitting and adjust it to their needs.
items.trafficsense_kotlin: Android and IoT experiment that reacts to live data. The app reads location updates, overlays routes on Google Maps, and suggests carpools to cut travel and exposure. A small rules engine chooses between route options based on traffic and shared pickups. I wrote the data layer in plain Kotlin so behavior is easy to follow, and I logged decisions to help tune the rules. It is a good starting point for mobility projects that want to try ideas quickly.
items.ndorokojo_kotlin: Livestock marketplace that keeps the flow simple. Sellers post a listing with a short form, buyers filter by type and location, and both sides get notifications when there is a match. OSMDroid handles the map so the app stays light. The list is optimized for low end phones and still feels responsive. I shipped a small admin tool to clear spam and keep the feed clean.
items.jukee_java: Music player in Java with a hosted playlist feature. Playlists sync with Firebase so a friend can load the same set in a few seconds. Playback is smooth with a simple service and a tidy notification, and the UI avoids heavy decoration so it stays fast. I wrote the storage layer with clear interfaces so switching to another backend would be straightforward. It is a solid example of a classic Android app that still feels good.
items.my_heavy_equipment_kotlin: Maintenance helper built for field use. It scans QR codes to pull an asset record, stores entries locally, and builds a PDF summary you can send to a supervisor. The REST API is small and predictable so it is easy to mock in tests. Offline work is queued and retried when the network returns. The screens avoid clutter and the flow keeps the user in a single context until the job is done.
items.beataco_java_swing: Desktop tool for Telegram broadcasts that favors control. You draft a message, pick targets, schedule a send, and watch a compact log for results. It talks to the Telegram Bot API and remembers basic settings between sessions. The UI is Swing with sensible defaults and keyboard shortcuts for operators who live on the app for hours. It is not flashy and that is the point.
items.beritain_kotlin: Android news app that aims for predictable behavior. The architecture is MVVM with strict module boundaries so features do not tangle. Articles are encrypted at rest with SQLCipher and dependencies are wired with Koin. Network calls are pinned and WorkManager handles background refresh. I tested empty states and bad network paths so the app fails in a way that still makes sense.
items.ecoquest_kotlin: Sustainability app with a light game layer. Users pick small quests, earn points, and see their place on a leaderboard. The stack is MVVM with Firebase for sync and simple analytics to learn which quests stick. Reminders are gentle and can be muted so it does not feel like spam. The UI uses accessible colors and large tap targets so it works well on older devices.
items.sakuku_kotlin: Personal finance app that tries to stay calm. Balances and goals are on one screen and you can drill down without losing context. I wrote small custom views for charts to avoid heavy dependencies and tuned them for low memory devices. Data syncs through Firebase which keeps setup light for a single user. The code is clean enough that a new contributor can add a screen in a day.
items.examine_kotlin: Scanner that treats security as part of the normal flow. Codes are read, payloads are encrypted with AES, and actions are tied to a device id for traceability. Retrofit handles requests and the audit trail is stored in a way that is easy to export. I added clear user prompts for failure cases so people do not get stuck. The end result is strict without feeling heavy.
items.hangman_java: Small hangman game for Android built for quick play. It runs fully offline and never nags. Word packs live in the app, progress is saved locally, and the UI is large and readable. The code shows a clean separation between the game loop and the view which makes it a nice teaching sample.
items.bankit_java: Banking style sample that demonstrates clear flows without extra noise. Login, transfer, and history use patterns that teams already know which makes it easy to extend. Lists and forms are tidy and the code is straight Java on purpose. It is a good base when you need to show a stakeholder what a simple path would look like.
items.laundry_compose: Compose UI for a laundry service that focuses on predictable components. Home, services, and order flow share one design system and all components have previews. State holders are thin, theming is consistent, and everything is ready to receive real endpoints. I measured a few large lists to keep scrolling fluid on budget phones.
items.picdf_compose: Tool that turns images into a single PDF with a short path. Pick photos, reorder with drag and drop, set a title, and export with PdfDocument. The app shows a share sheet right after the file is written, and it keeps a small recent list for quick access. The code avoids hidden work on the main thread so the UI stays responsive during export.
items.aromaloka_kotlin: UI slicing project that matches a reference layout closely. ConstraintLayout handles dense parts and MotionLayout adds small transitions where they help. I wrote notes in the code about spacing and ratios so handoff is simple. The goal was not to reinvent the design but to ship a faithful layout that engineers can build on.
items.diabetless_kotlin: Healthcare UI slicing that values calm and clarity. Forms use clear labels and input masks to reduce mistakes, and color choices follow accessibility targets. Navigation is shallow and error messages point to the exact field. The structure matches common patterns so real endpoints can drop in without reshuffling everything.
items.painthings_kotlin: Art marketplace slicing with attention to images. There is a grid, a detail view with a clean gallery, a simple cart, and a fake checkout so flows can be tested end to end. Image loading is smooth and the layout scales down to small screens. The point was to keep the visuals in front and keep the forms from getting in the way.
items.capstone_kotlin: Concept app that ties a few screens into a believable flow. Navigation is straightforward, view models own state, and repositories isolate data access. The project includes a small fake backend so people can click through without setting up services. It is the kind of base you can demo at the end of a sprint and then keep.
items.cba_java: Beauty shop UI in Java that covers the usual path. Product list, details, cart, and a small coupon step are in place. SQLite caches responses so the app feels quick after the first run. The code follows standard Android patterns and avoids heavy libraries so it is easy to read.
items.gamography_swiftui: Game catalog for iOS with a clean SwiftUI front end. Search and favorites work offline, images load with async pipelines, and the network layer is thin so a new API can be swapped in without stress. I tuned list performance for older phones and built a couple of accessibility tweaks for large text. It feels fast yet still readable.
items.fmv_pcr_multiplatform: PCR diagnostic app built with Kotlin Multiplatform and Jetpack Compose, running natively on Android, iOS, and Desktop from a single shared codebase. The app pairs with the PCR device over BLE to start runs, stream real-time amplification curves, and display interpreted results. Shared domain logic covers device handshake, protocol parsing, result calculation, and offline caching, while Compose Multiplatform renders identical, high-fidelity UI across all three targets. The MVVM and Clean Architecture layers keep BLE communication strictly separate from presentation, making it straightforward to extend for new device variants without touching the UI.
items.cvdetect_multiplatform: CVDetect is a Kotlin Multiplatform app with Jetpack Compose that performs cardiovascular screening by connecting to the CVDetect medical device over BLE. Shared business logic handles device discovery, measurement session management, waveform capture, and AI-assisted risk interpretation. Compose Multiplatform delivers a consistent, platform-native interface on Android and iOS, while the Clean Architecture structure isolates BLE communication from the clinical workflow UI, ensuring reliable operation even when the network is unavailable.
items.lunit_folder_uploader: Desktop GUI tool built with Python and PySide6 for batch-uploading medical image folders to the Lunit 4T4TB platform. The interface lets operators select a root folder, preview the directory tree, configure upload settings, and monitor per-file progress in real time. Background workers handle the upload queue so the UI stays responsive during large transfers, and a built-in log panel captures errors with enough context to retry failed items without restarting the whole batch.
items.fmv_kiosk_website: Product landing page for the Digihealth Health Kiosk built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The page presents the kiosk's feature set, connected device integrations, and clinical workflow with animated sections, responsive layout for desktop and mobile, and locale-aware content that switches instantly without a page reload.
items.fmv_xray_website: Product landing page for the Digihealth X-Ray application built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The page showcases DICOM viewing, annotation tools, and offline-first workflow with clear visual sections, smooth scroll animations, and full localization that adapts content and layout direction for each language.
items.fmv_stethoscope_website: Product landing page for the Digital Stethoscope app built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The page highlights BLE pairing, real-time waveform visualization, and patient record attachment with an animated hero, feature cards, and seamless language switching across all three locales.
items.fmv_pcr_website: Product landing page for the PCR device built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The page presents the device's nucleic acid amplification workflow, rapid on-site diagnostic capabilities, and clinical use cases with an animated hero, feature highlights, and seamless language switching across all three locales.
items.fmv_fundoscope_website: Product landing page for the Fundoscope device built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The page walks through the device's retinal imaging capabilities, AI-assisted screening workflow, and clinical integration points with a clean visual hierarchy and locale-aware copy.
items.fmv_pathology_website: Product landing page for the Digital Pathology system built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The page presents whole-slide imaging, AI annotation assistance, and remote consultation features using responsive image grids, animated statistics, and full trilingual localization.
items.fmv_spirometer_website: Product landing page for the Spirometer device built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The page covers pulmonary function testing workflow, real-time flow-volume loop display, and reporting features with a crisp layout and instant language switching.
items.fmv_ecg_website: Product landing page for the ECG device built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The page presents 12-lead ECG capture, AI interpretation, and EHR export capabilities with animated waveform visuals, feature highlights, and full localization across all three languages.
items.fmv_enzyme_website: Product landing page for the Enzyme analyzer built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The page details rapid enzyme assay workflows, sample-to-result timing, and device integration with clean section layouts and locale-aware content.
items.fmv_epc_website: Product landing page for the EPC device built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The page outlines the device's diagnostic capabilities, integration with the Digihealth platform, and clinical use cases with responsive design and seamless trilingual support.
items.gtt_nano_website: Corporate website for GTT Nano built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The site covers the company's nanotechnology products, research capabilities, and partnership enquiry flow with a modern design, smooth scroll transitions, and full localization.
items.pcr_for_pets_website: Product landing page for PCR for Pets built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The page presents veterinary PCR diagnostics, species-specific test panels, and clinic integration with approachable visual design and locale-aware copy for three languages.
items.pets_healthcare_website: Company website for a pets healthcare brand built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The site showcases veterinary services, wellness programs, and booking flow with a warm visual style, responsive layout, and seamless language switching.
items.sugar_company_website: Corporate website for a sugar company built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The site presents production capacity, product lines, certifications, and partnership contacts with a clean industrial aesthetic and full trilingual localization.
items.fujian_medical_website: Corporate website for Fujian Medical Engineering built with Vue, Tailwind CSS, and vue-i18n supporting English, Indonesian, and Chinese. The site covers medical equipment solutions, engineering services, and regional distribution with a professional layout, responsive grid sections, and complete localization across all three languages.
